I'm a bit weary of changing the breakout last minute and loosing people 😅 But, let's see how people respond...! <@278099318647422977> <@292230513177919488> <@516571617686716426> <@695340005505106091> <@543900561460822016> <@583892532644151312> <@689161464829050960> <@273808422753796097> <@301186049323958275> can you: 1️⃣ join the call at a new time: 14 UTC tomorrow (Feb 27) 2️⃣ join at the currently scheduled time (14 UTC Feb 28) 3️⃣ join ACDE this Thursday Feb 29 14 UTC <@552133098075193354> there's no EIP for it yet, but can we discuss the alias-origin-to-sender topic as well? Maybe that's something small and digestible that can make it into Pectra? First AA baby step. if we have the time, then I imagine that would fall in the "other alternatives/proposals" bucket, but I think it's worth making sure we get the first point right and spend as much time as needed on it before going into specifics > 2938 has an even lower chance, considering that it is vulnerable to builder DoS vectors that are mitigated by 7560 and 4337 but would be hard to mitigate in 2938 Could you (or anyone) refresh my memory on this DoS? It's been a long time since I've thought about AA 😅 IIRC, 2938 had similar mempool rules to those proposed in 7562 and does separate execution into pre- and post-`PAYGAS` sections. The main issue is that validation and execution are a single transaction. This means that if you accepted 10 transactions into the mempool, the first might invalidate the rest, so you must re-evaluate each transaction after each transaction inclusion. In addition, the validation logic restrictions (before the PAYGAS opcode) are much more restrictive than 7562, and prevent most use-cases supported by it (storage rules, and paymasters) Ah, I see. The suggested mempool rules in 2938 only keep one transaction per account for exactly that reason, which is quite limiting. its not even one transaction per account - one account's code might invalidate the validation of the next account... Hm, even with: > If the execution hits [...] an external call/create that changes the callee to anything but the target or a precompile [exit with failure] ? I don't mean to argue though, the rules in 2938 are _extremely_ strict. tx1 validates itself, but its execution (which is unrestricted) modifies the validation of tx2. so tx1 and tx2 are valid (separately), but once tx1 is executed, tx2 can't be put into the same block. The major thing we've done in erc7562 with erc4337 is that all validation (under their restrictions) are done before all executions. This way, the unrestricted execution code of all transaction can't invalidate (can cause reverts, of course, but the transactions are all already pre-paid) How would tx2 "see" the modifications of tx1 without the balance or call/ext families of instructions? Keep in mind that 2938 has the `AA_PREFIX` that prevents normal calls Given the high number of responses here for Wed + Thur, and low-ish for tomorrow, let's keep the breakout on Wednesday and allocate some time on ACDE Thursday to recap + hear from people who can't make it on Wed (cc: <@727296082484265073>)
